primitives.name: Spatiotemporal Transformer Decoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: Instead of generating words as in natural language processing, temporal player and ball movements can be generated by training a transformer model to predict the next position from a sequence of tracking data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'sequence length (dimensionless)', 'O_{\\tau,n}': 'object token at time τ for entity n (position px,py,pz; velocity vx,vy,vz; distance dx,dy,dz; elapsed time e)'}
primitives.assumptions: Player and ball motion follows a learnable temporal pattern; object tokens encode sufficient kinematic and relational features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Prediction error increases with time beyond training horizon due to chaotic dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Maps sequential tracking data into probabilistic motion forecasts using attention-based recurrence.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and ground-truth ball/player positions over time.

primitives.name: Probabilistic Match Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: We show that the model output sampling parameters are crucial to simulation realism and that SportsNGEN is probabilistically well-calibrated to real data.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{sim}(x_t | x_{<t})': 'probability density of simulated state x_t given history x_{<t}', 'p_{real}(x_t)': 'empirical distribution of real match states'}
primitives.assumptions: Match evolution is governed by stochastic processes; simulations must align with empirical distributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when sampling parameters misalign with real-world variability.

layer2.mapping: Simulated match states mirror real-world statistical properties via calibrated probabilistic sampling.
layer2.telemetry: Kullback-Leibler divergence between simulated and real match statistics.

primitives.name: Customizable Player Modeling
primitives.verbatim_quote: In addition, a generic version of SportsNGEN can be customized to a specific player by fine-tuning on the subset of match data that includes that player.

primitives.assumptions: Individual player behavior can be captured via transfer learning from shared dataset.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting risk when D_{player} is too small or non-representative.

layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of simulated shots vs. actual shot selection for target player.

SportsNGEN operates by training a transformer decoder on spatiotemporal tracking data, enabling generation of sustained gameplay sequences. The core mechanism involves predicting next positions from prior sequences, which requires encoding object tokens (players/ball) with kinematic features such as position, velocity, and relative distances. These tokens form a temporal sequence that the model learns to extend probabilistically. The system's realism hinges on its ability to maintain statistical fidelity over time, achieved through careful calibration of sampling parameters. As time progresses, prediction errors accumulate due to inherent unpredictability in sports dynamics—this limits deterministic forecasting but supports probabilistic modeling. The architecture supports customization via fine-tuning on individual player datasets, allowing for tailored behavioral simulations. This dual capability enables both general-purpose and specialized match simulation, forming the basis for strategic analysis and coaching tools.
